chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: That year, 419, the dikes of Keba gave way and the sea came in. A flood of complaints reached the court.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In 424, work began on the granary at Draeziatam.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: That year, 426, a flood of pilgrims came to Keba for the feast. The tail of the procession stretched to the river.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: Be it remembered that in the year 429 Queen Riaeirn went the way of all flesh and was laid to rest in Breskind.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: Be it remembered that in the year 439 the heavens shut their doors over Pexiarwyth and not a drop fell all summer.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year of grace 442, merchants from Riamur filled the squares of Steiork with silk and pepper.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: Be it remembered that in the year 443 the heavens shut their doors over Deizerk and not a drop fell all summer. The abbot fell sick in the winter.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: Year 444. Pilgrims at Keba.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In the year 444, a flood of pilgrims came to Keba for the feast. The star of the house of Loulask was rising at court.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In the year 444, a great fire broke out in Breskind and the guildhall was lost.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In the year 454, Queen Paskasesk died and was buried at Steiork. The chronicler's hand grew weary.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In the year 456, a storm from the sea drove the waves over the shore at Dretyrk.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: That year, 457, Queen Paskasesk died and was buried at Heidomask.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: Be it remembered that in the year 465 Queen Paskasesk went the way of all flesh and was laid to rest in Kubryterk. The tail of the procession stretched to the river.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year of grace 468, Draeziatam shut its gates against Queen Paskasesk and the bells rang for rebellion.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In the year 468, the people of Draeziatam (called Tholaevol by others) rose against Queen Paskasesk.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year of grace 471, the Breitugask swelled like a wrathful beast and swallowed the meadows of Sonobun.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In the year 471, envoys came from Riamur bearing gifts for Queen Nuzaern.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In the year 471, the Breitugask burst its banks and drowned the fields of Sonobun.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: Year 472. Pestilence at Kubryterk.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: That year, 473, snow lay on the banks of the Bostaem (called Kiarend by others) until the month of flowers. A two-headed calf was born at Riamur.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year 484 of the Reckoning, a white broom of fire swept the heavens over the dawn ridge for ten nights.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year of grace 484, Prince Grenyx met the host of Festei by Riamur, and won the field. The bells were recast.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In the year 491, Prince Grenyx fought the men of Wosel at Hougoun and was driven back.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: That year, 493, the sun grew dark and stars showed at noon.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In the year 496, the dikes of Steiork gave way and the sea came in.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: Year 501. Revolt at Lipaskthen.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year of grace 501, Kubryterk shut its gates against Prince Grenyx and the bells rang for rebellion.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: Year 516. Pestilence at Grouka.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In 516, the granaries of Keba stood empty. There was hunger for war among the young lords.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In the year 530, the wells of Keba ran dry.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In 532, fire burned the lower town of Keba. Some say this happened a year later.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: Be it remembered that in the year 541 the masons of Steiork raised the guildhall to the glory of heaven.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In 547, Duke Gifaeth fought the men of Festei at Ougux and was driven back. The tower clock stopped and was mended.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: Year 549. Fair at Rogrouv (called Steiork by others). Grain was cheap that year.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: Year 550. Rogrouv burned. The guildhall lost. The bells were recast.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In 550, the waters of the Thatham rose higher than any could remember and covered Sonobun.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In 565, envoys came from Riamur bearing gifts for Duke Gifaeth.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In 568, Duke Gifaeth fought the men of Ideives at Hougoun and lost many men.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In 568, a great fair was held at Heidomask, and merchants came from Akrol.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year 569 of the Reckoning, the Breitugask forgot its bed and wandered over Pexiarwyth, drowning the sheaves.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year of grace 571, the Breitugask (called Nougreind by others) swelled like a wrathful beast and swallowed the meadows of Pexiarwyth.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: Year 586. Red moon over Sazouv (called Keba by others).

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year 591, a silver light like a torch hung above the morning sea for twelve nights.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: That year, 591, a snowy light like a torch hung where the day is born for twelve nights.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: That year, 592, snow lay on the banks of the Thatham until the month of flowers.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year 593 of the Reckoning, death walked the streets of Draeziatam (called Tholaevol by others) with a full sack.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: In 610, Duke Nyorkgand took a wife from Brerdrom.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year of grace 611, the moon put on a robe of blood above Keba. The star of the house of Kradrebath was rising at court.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: In 612, work began on the cathedral at Kubryterk.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year 612 of the Reckoning, the masons of Kubryterk (called Lipaskthen by others) raised the watchtower to the glory of heaven.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: In 615, a great fire broke out in Heidomask (called Pysahiax by others) and the granary was lost. The star of the house of Briem was rising at court.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: That year, 618, Duke Nyorkgand fought the men of Ideives at Brerdrom and won the field. The old well was cleaned.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: 620. Red moon over Pysahiax. There was hunger for war among the young lords.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: Be it remembered that in the year 621 flames ate the roofs of Draeziatam from one gate to the other.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: Be it remembered that in the year 623 the Bostaem forgot its bed and wandered over Pexiarwyth, drowning the sheaves.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In 623, the waters of the Bostaem (called Kiarend by others) rose higher than any could remember and covered Pexiarwyth. Grain was cheap that year.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In the year 626, Duke Nyorkgand died and was buried at Kubryterk. A flood of complaints reached the court.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: In the year of grace 628, Duke Nyorkgand was wed to a daughter of Briagri, and there was feasting for a week.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year 634 of the Reckoning, the moon put on a robe of blood above Steiork. The tower clock stopped and was mended.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year of grace 634, merchants from Akrol filled the squares of Draeziatam with silk and pepper.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: Year 636. Red moon over Sazouv. Some say this happened a year later.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: Be it remembered that in the year 638 flames ate the roofs of Draeziatam from one gate to the other.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: In 640, the wells of Kubryterk ran dry.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year of grace 640, the heavens shut their doors over Pexiarwyth and not a drop fell all summer.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year of grace 643, the masons of Kubryterk raised the great hall to the glory of heaven.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: In the year 651, Duke Wekrund took a wife from Briagri.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: Be it remembered that in the year 651 Duke Wekrund was wed to a daughter of Hougoun, and there was feasting for a week. The old well was cleaned.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: Year 652. Sickness in Pexiarwyth.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: That year, 656, a pestilence came to Steiork and many died. The old well was cleaned.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: Be it remembered that in the year 662 flames ate the roofs of Kubryterk (called Lipaskthen by others) from one gate to the other. A two-headed calf was born at Brerdrom.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year of grace 664, Duke Zadyr met the host of Wosel by Riamur, and lost many men.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: Be it remembered that in the year 671 the masons of Keba raised the watchtower to the glory of heaven. The tail of the procession stretched to the river.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: 673. Sea in at Kubryterk. Many said it was an omen.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In 673, the sea broke the dikes at Kubryterk and salt water covered the fields.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: Year 684. No rain. Wells of Grouka dry. Many said it was an omen.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: In 684, the people of Breskind went away to seek new land.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: In 685, a great fire broke out in Breskind and the granary was lost. A flood of complaints reached the court.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: 699. Bearded light towards the sunrise. chalky. 11 nights. The price of salt rose.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: In 699, a great storm came out of the sea and broke the boats at Bernhovou. Grain was cheap that year.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: 700. Dikes broken at Pysahiax.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year 700 of the Reckoning, Duke Sekork met the host of Festei by Ougux, and won the field.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: 701. Pysahiax emptied. Grain was cheap that year.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year 701 of the Reckoning, want sat at every table in Steiork, and mothers boiled grass for their children. Many said it was an omen.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year 701, the granaries of Steiork stood empty. The old well was cleaned.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In 701, there was a great dearth of bread in Deizerk.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In the year 706, a flood of pilgrims came to Keba for the feast.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In the year 709, the granaries of Kubryterk stood empty.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: That year, 723, there was hunger in Steiork, and the poor ate bark. Many said it was an omen.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year 730 of the Reckoning, winter laid an iron hand on the land and the Bostaem became a road of ice.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In the year 732, the people of Breskind rose against King Breswiar.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: That year, 737, King Breswiar died and was buried at Draeziatam. The tail of the procession stretched to the river.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: Be it remembered that in the year 740 merchants from Akrol filled the squares of Breskind with silk and pepper.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: Year 746. King Breswiar married. Some say this happened a year later.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: In the year 747, stars were seen falling low over the midday sea like rain.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: Be it remembered that in the year 747 King Breswiar went the way of all flesh and was laid to rest in Draeziatam.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In the year 747, many stars fell from the sky in one night.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: 748. Hard winter on the Thaebrouth.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year 749 of the Reckoning, death walked the streets of Draeziatam with a full sack. The tower clock stopped and was mended.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: 751. Drought in Volu.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: That year, 751, the new bridge over the Bostaem (called Kiarend by others) was finished.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: That year, 760, salt spoiled the fields of Breskind and nothing grew.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: Year 770. Prince Viapulkusk married. Some say this happened a year later.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: In the year 780 of the Reckoning, the Nougreind swelled like a wrathful beast and swallowed the meadows of Volu (called Pexiarwyth by others).

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: That year, 785, the moon rose red over Breskind.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: 786. Harvest failed, Tonbrux. Some say this happened a year later.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In 786, the harvest failed in Sonobun. Wolves were seen near Ougux.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: Be it remembered that in the year 789 flames ate the roofs of Keba from one gate to the other.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Pysahiax
text: Year 793. Lipaskthen emptied. A flood of complaints reached the court.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: That year, 793, work began on the abbey church at Breskind (called Grouka by others).

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Pysahiax
text: 795. Stars fell.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: Year 795. Fair at Rogrouv.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year of grace 795, it seemed the sky itself was weeping stars towards the desert quarter.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: Be it remembered that in the year 798 it seemed the sky itself was weeping stars towards the cold quarter.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year 799 of the Reckoning, Duke Petheges went the way of all flesh and was laid to rest in Keba. A two-headed calf was born at Akrol.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In 800, the winter was hard and the Bostaem froze from bank to bank. The bells were recast.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: 801. Sun darkened at noon.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Pysahiax
text: Year 804. Bearded light towards the setting sun. ruddy. 3 nights. The old well was cleaned.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: Be it remembered that in the year 804 a silver broom of fire swept the heavens towards the sunrise for eleven nights.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: That year, 810, Duke Petheges took a wife from Akrol. Some say this happened a year later.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: 810. Duke Petheges married. The abbot fell sick in the winter.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: 818. Eclipse.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In the year 818, the sun grew dark and stars showed at noon.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: That year, 821, Queen Zizougel fought the men of Ideives at Akrol and made a truce.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: Year 834. No harvest at Grouka. Wolves were seen near Hougoun.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In the year 834, the harvest failed in Deizerk.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: That year, 838, Queen Zizougel fought the men of Ideives at Briagri and lost many men. The chronicler's hand grew weary.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Pysahiax
text: 847. Watchtower begun at Sazouv. The abbot fell sick in the winter.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: 847. Hunger at Lipaskthen (called Kubryterk by others). There was hunger for war among the young lords.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In the year 847, work began on the abbey church at Keba.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In 849, work began on the guildhall at Draeziatam. A two-headed calf was born at Akrol.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: Year 858. Harvest failed, Volu.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: 859. Kiarend over its banks.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: 866. Pilgrims at Sazouv.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Pysahiax
text: 868. No harvest at Rogrouv. A two-headed calf was born at Akrol.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: Year 872. Bridge over the Thaebrouth finished.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: Year 872. Bridge over the Thaebrouth (called Thatham by others) finished.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: Be it remembered that in the year 881 the heavens shut their doors over Deizerk and not a drop fell all summer. A two-headed calf was born at Ougux.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: 882. Fire at Grouka.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: In 882, a great fire broke out in Breskind and the watchtower was lost.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: Year 888. Breitugask over its banks.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: In the year 889, the moon was red as blood above Breskind.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Pysahiax
text: Year 892. Flood on the Nougreind. Giasel under water.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: Year 892. Pilgrims at Tholaevol. There was hunger for war among the young lords.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: That year, 896, a cloud of earthen grasshoppers settled on Deizerk (called Giasel by others). Some say this happened a year later.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: 899. Lipaskthen burned. The watchtower lost. The old well was cleaned.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: That year, 904, envoys came from Riamur bearing gifts for Queen Ubam.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: 907. Fair at Pysahiax. Many said it was an omen.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: Year 909. Bearded light over the dawn ridge. silver. 10 nights.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: Be it remembered that in the year 909 a snowy broom of fire swept the heavens over the dawn ridge for ten nights.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: 912. Prince Ohoux married. A flood of complaints reached the court.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In 914, Prince Ohoux died and was buried at Keba.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Pysahiax
text: 918. Envoys from Akrol.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: Year 923. Fire at Lipaskthen. Wolves were seen near Ougux.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year of grace 931, Prince Ohoux met the host of Wosel by Hougoun, and made a truce. Nothing else of note.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: Year 932. Folk of Grouka left for the hills.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: In the year 934, stars were seen falling in the north like rain.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Pysahiax
text: Be it remembered that in the year 936 the sea rose up in anger against Daskeim and the boats were split like kindling. Some say this happened a year later.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year 936 of the Reckoning, the sea rose up in anger against Dretyrk and the boats were split like kindling.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: 939. Sea storm, Daskeim.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: Be it remembered that in the year 941 death walked the streets of Steiork with a full sack.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: In 941, King Bregaen died and was buried at Heidomask. Nothing else of note.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: 953. Sickness in Giasel.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: Be it remembered that in the year 957 Duke Vyeiark went the way of all flesh and was laid to rest in Heidomask.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Pysahiax
text: Year 961. Envoys from Brerdrom.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: In the year 964, a great fair was held at Steiork, and merchants came from Brerdrom.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Pysahiax
text: 966. Nougreind over its banks.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In the year 966, the waters of the Breitugask rose higher than any could remember and covered Sonobun (called Tonbrux by others).

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: That year, 967, snow lay on the banks of the Thatham until the month of flowers.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: 968. Pestilence at Tholaevol (called Draeziatam by others). Wolves were seen near Ougux.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: 975. Pilgrims at Lipaskthen.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: Year 982. Locusts, earthen, in Volu.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: Year 989. Bridge over the Nougreind finished.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: In 990, the waters of the Breitugask rose higher than any could remember and covered Deizerk. The tower clock stopped and was mended.

chronicler: the Town Book of Draeziatam
text: In 1007, a storm from the sea drove the waves over the shore at Bernhovou (called Oubomond by others).

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Pysahiax
text: Year 1008. Sea in at Pysahiax.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: That year, 1009, many families left Heidomask for the hills. A two-headed calf was born at Briagri.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Pysahiax
text: 1014. Battle at Riamur with Ideives; Prince Naeldskouv was driven back. The tail of the procession stretched to the river.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: Year 1014. Battle at Ougux with Ideives; Prince Naeldskouv lost many men.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: 1032. Great frost. Kiarend (called Bostaem by others) frozen.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: That year, 1033, a great fair was held at Keba, and merchants came from Brerdrom. A two-headed calf was born at Brerdrom.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Pysahiax
text: 1037. Sun darkened at noon.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: In the year 1038, many stars fell from the sky in one night. The tower clock stopped and was mended.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Lipaskthen
text: 1041. Earthquake at Tholaevol.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: In 1048, a great fair was held at Steiork, and merchants came from Briagri.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: 1048. Battle at Ougux with Ideives; Queen Tousty made a truce. The bells were recast.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: 1049. Queen Tousty married. Grain was cheap that year.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Pysahiax
text: 1057. Sickness in Giasel.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: Year 1061. Duke Mumnegrysk married.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year 1064 of the Reckoning, Duke Mumnegrysk met the host of Wosel by Riamur, and was driven back.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Lipaskthen
text: 1081. Pestilence at Pysahiax.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: In the year of grace 1106, it seemed the sky itself was weeping stars where the day goes down.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Lipaskthen
text: Year 1109. Nougreind over its banks.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Lipaskthen
text: In the year 1114 of the Reckoning, merchants from Riamur filled the squares of Rogrouv (called Steiork by others) with silk and pepper.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Lipaskthen
text: In the year 1115 of the Reckoning, flames ate the roofs of Rogrouv from one gate to the other.

chronicler: the Town Book of Draeziatam
text: That year, 1118, the winter was hard and the Thatham froze from bank to bank.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: Year 1119. Pestilence at Tholaevol.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: Year 1131. Duke Thonedriax married. The price of salt rose.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: In 1137, stars were seen falling over the evening hills like rain.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: 1154. Guildhall begun at Tholaevol (called Draeziatam by others).

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: Year 1155. Pilgrims at Grouka.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Pysahiax
text: Year 1156. Great frost. Nougreind frozen.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: In the year of grace 1158, it seemed the sky itself was weeping stars in the north. The tower clock stopped and was mended.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year of grace 1161, Keba (called Sazouv by others) shut its gates against King Stukuld and the bells rang for rebellion.

chronicler: the Town Book of Draeziatam
text: Year 1178. Envoys from Riamur.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: In 1194, the coughing sickness spread through Sonobun.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: That year, 1200, Queen Zyzifaern fought the men of Festei at Brerdrom and lost many men.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: Year 1201. Tholaevol (called Draeziatam by others) burned. The abbey church lost.

chronicler: the Town Book of Draeziatam
text: In 1201, work began on the watchtower at Kubryterk (called Lipaskthen by others). The abbot fell sick in the winter.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Pysahiax
text: Year 1214. Eclipse.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: 1214. Sun darkened at noon. The tail of the procession stretched to the river.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In 1216, a great storm came out of the sea and broke the boats at Bernhovou.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Lipaskthen
text: Year 1217. Drought in Giasel.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: In 1217, the dikes of Heidomask gave way and the sea came in.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: In the year 1217, no rain fell in Deizerk from spring to autumn. There was hunger for war among the young lords.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year 1217, the winter was hard and the Thatham froze from bank to bank. The price of salt rose.

chronicler: the Town Book of Draeziatam
text: That year, 1217, earthen hoppers rose out of the ground in Deizerk and stripped the fields.
